identity.name: Upper Egypt
alt_names: Southern kingdom of the First Intermediate Period

land.text: the nome of Thebes, whose nomarch Intef the Elder was 'keeper of the Door of the South'

predecessors.note: The Theban nomarchs were governors under the Old Kingdom; the state is recorded from the infobox 'Thebes (c. 2134 BC - c. 2061 BC), Eleventh Dynasty'. Counterpart in the ledger is 'nobody' because the southern nomes had passed to their nomarchs (see old-kingdom-of-egypt).

land.text: the Theban kingdom from Elephantine north to Abydos and the edge of Middle Egypt

successors.note: The Theban kingdom continues unbroken under Mentuhotep II, who 'ascended the Theban throne in 2055 BC' (Middle Kingdom page); the split into two dossiers follows Cliopatria's two rows.

capitals.name: Thebes (Waset; Luxor)
capitals.note: Page infobox 'Thebes (c. 2134 BC - c. 2061 BC), Eleventh Dynasty'; the dossier runs it to the Middle Kingdom start in 2055.

correction.text: the nome of Thebes under Intef the Elder, 'keeper of the Door of the South', and the first Theban kings: the page gives no territory and says only that rule was 'roughly equally divided between two competing power bases'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws a 19,657 km2 Upper Egypt (Elephantine to lat 27.4) from -2200. The page dates Thebes only from c. 2134 BC and has Thebes win Nekhen and expand 'toward Elephantine' only 'by around 2060 BC', and the Abydos conquest later still; before that Ankhtifi, nomarch of Hierakonpolis, was a rival to the south. So the full shape is wrong for -2200..-2101 and the Theban core (radius 50 km, confidence 1: the page gives no extent) is used from -2134. -2200..-2135 has no state (nomarchs, see old-kingdom-of-egypt).

correction.text: the nome of Thebes, as in the previous keyframe, until Nekhen and Abydos are won

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's second shape is the same 19,657 km2; the page's southern and northern conquests come at the very end of the Theban kingdom's independent life (c. 2061-2060 BC). Years cut to -2100..-2062, shape replaced by the Theban core.

correction.text: Thebes after the conquest of Nekhen and Abydos: Elephantine north to Abydos, short of Siut

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe from Cliopatria's Upper Egypt shape (Elephantine to lat 27.4) minus the Asyut governorate: the page has Intef II defeat 'the governor of Nekhen, allowing further expansion south, toward Elephantine' and Intef III complete 'the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt', while Siut stayed a northern 'buffer state' until Mentuhotep II. Page gives no area; 19.7k km2 for the full shape is plausible for this strip.

region.text: Thebes: 'Thebes (c. 2134 BC - c. 2061 BC), Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt'

ledger.note: c. 2134 BC: the Theban Eleventh Dynasty begins in Upper Egypt. Infobox 'Thebes (c. 2134 BC - c. 2061 BC), Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt'; Intef the Elder was 'the nomarch of Thebes, often called the keeper of the Door of the South', who 'did not appear to have tried to claim the title of king'. The page names the city, not a boundary, hence the radius (confidence 2 for year and place; the extent is the researcher's).

c. 2069 BC: Thebes attacks Abydos. 'One of them, Intef II, begins the assault on the north, particularly at Abydos.' No year on the page; placed at the start of Intef III's reign in the infobox ('c. 2069 BC - c. 2061 BC').

region.text: Abydos, 'the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt'

ledger.note: c. 2061 BC: Intef III takes Abydos. 'His successor, Intef III, completed the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt against the Heracleopolitan kings.' Undated on the page; placed at the end of the Theban dynasty's c. 2061 BC date.
c. 2061 BC: the Abydos fighting ends with the Theban conquest.

region.text: Nekhen (Hierakonpolis) and the way 'south, toward Elephantine'

ledger.note: By c. 2060 BC (placed in -2061): Thebes defeats the governor of Nekhen and extends to Elephantine. 'By around 2060 BC, Intef II had defeated the governor of Nekhen, allowing further expansion south, toward Elephantine.' The Aswan governorate is the researcher's reading of 'toward Elephantine'. Counterpart nobody (reviewer me-03-a): the governor of Nekhen's nome is not a state with a dossier, as for the Old Kingdom's -2181 loss of the south to its nomarchs. Ankhtifi, an earlier nomarch of Hierakonpolis, 'tried to expand to the north to conquer the nome centred on Thebes, but was unsuccessful' (undated).

region.text: the Theban kingdom, continuing as the Middle Kingdom

ledger.note: c. 2055 BC: the Theban kingdom becomes the Middle Kingdom. 'The struggle was to be concluded by Mentuhotep II, who ascended the Theban throne in 2055 BC' (Middle Kingdom page); the First Intermediate Period page ends the period 'c. 2055 BC'. Same state under the Middle Kingdom's name; the conquest of the north follows in 2033.

wars.name: Theban-Heracleopolitan war
wars.outcome: Intef II began the assault on Abydos and Intef III completed its conquest; the war goes on under Mentuhotep II (see lower-egypt and middle-kingdom-of-egypt).
wars.note: Dates are the Intef III reign in the infobox and the Theban end c. 2061; no battle is dated.

wars.name: Ankhtifi's attack on Thebes
wars.outcome: Ankhtifi, nomarch of Hierakonpolis, 'tried to expand to the north to conquer the nome centred on Thebes, but was unsuccessful'; Thebes later beat the governor of Nekhen (c. 2060 BC).
wars.note: Undated on the page; the span is the Theban dynasty's years before the Nekhen victory, shown only so the reviewer can see it was considered.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders; the Theban core and the later strip are approximate. Siut is a buffer on the northern side.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Upper Egypt' (-2200..-2001; two identical 19,657 km2 shapes from Elephantine to lat 27.4) is the Theban kingdom of the First Intermediate Period. This dossier IS the 'Thebes' rival the group scope says Cliopatria lacks; me-03-x need not write it. CONFLICT WITH CLIOPATRIA: Cliopatria draws the whole Elephantine-to-Siut strip as one state from -2200; the page shows only Thebes from c. 2134, Nekhen and Elephantine won around 2060 and Abydos after, so the full shape is used only from -2061 and the Theban core before it (confidence 1). The state is the same as the Middle Kingdom from 2055 (Thebes continues unbroken): a merge candidate for the colour agent. The page's chronology is internally uncertain: Intef III (c. 2069-2061) is said to succeed Intef II, who defeated Nekhen 'by around 2060'; Mentuhotep II's stela is 'ca. 2051-2030' and the defeat of the north 'around 2033'. The page does not mention Thinis, Coptos, Dendera, Gebelein or Armant. NOT DRAWN: nothing about Nubia. Natural Earth Aswan governorate is used for the southern gain (it also covers desert to the Red Sea); Elephantine is the gazetteer's Aswan.
